payload.report: An 81-year-old man with cough, fever, dyspnea and right Horner's syndrome has right upper lobe consolidation, positive Blastomyces urine antigen, and BAL GMS showing broad-based budding yeast, with negative TB, cryptococcus, legionella, and influenza tests. The radiologist notes that Histoplasma antigen cross-reacts with Blastomyces, favoring blastomycosis over histoplasmosis. Horner's syndrome is best explained by apical inflammatory scarring from pulmonary blastomycosis, supported by no mass and normal head imaging. Therefore the diagnosis is disseminated pulmonary blastomycosis; pulmonary malignancy and cardioembolic vascular event remain very unlikely.
